questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.description:

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

"""Prove the global TypeSafe API key resolves and the System One API answers.

There is deliberately no python-dotenv here. The key is meant to be available
globally from the environment (macOS Keychain -> ~/.zshenv -> every zsh), so
reading anything other than os.environ would hide a broken setup.

Run:  python smoke_test.py
"""

import os
import sys

REQUIRED_VAR = "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"


def require_key() -> None:
    if os.environ.get(REQUIRED_VAR):
        return
    print(f"{REQUIRED_VAR} is not set in this environment.\n", file=sys.stderr)
    print("Fix it in this order:", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  1. Run ./setup_global_key.sh in Terminal.app (not through Claude Code).", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  2. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it", file=sys.stderr)
    print("     started with, so it will not see the new variable until restarted.", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  3. Check status any time with ./setup_global_key.sh --check", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main() -> int:
    require_key()

    try:
        from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        print("typesafe-sdk is not installed. Run:  pip install typesafe-sdk", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # The client picks the key up from TYPESAFE_API_KEY on its own.
    with TypeSafeClient() as client:
        response = client.system_one(
            state={"document": "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP."},

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 013 is the latest, so the next
  one is 014. `docs/STATUS.md` holds the current number.
- The proposed Jev recruiting pilot is captured in
  `docs/2026-09-22-jev-recruiting-pilot.md`. It is a shadow-mode plan, not an
  approved workbook rule or a replacement for the weekly refresh.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

# AGENTS.md

Project: CFB_Playoff_Benchmarks

## What this is
Two linked questions about Baylor Football, answered from the full Power Four population.
First: for each game and season, what does bad, average, good and elite output look like,
where elite means the numbers College Football Playoff teams actually put up. Second: how
many wins does the playoff take, what metric profile earns that many wins, and what is
Baylor's gap on each metric. Python and DuckDB pipeline on CFBD play-by-play, 2021 to 2025
as the reference, 2026 scored live. Audience order: Applied Performance staff, then
coaches, then personnel. Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-cfb-playoff-benchmarks-design.md`.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- The DuckDB file is local to the Mac, gitignored, and never inside a cloud-synced folder. Machines exchange Parquet snapshots through Drive, as the PFF and GPS pipelines do.
- Every fact row carries `source_system` and `pulled_at`. Metric definitions live in one YAML, never in code.
- Tests use fixtures and mocked HTTP. No test touches the live API or the real DB.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

description: "Drive mount reads hang; DEFAULT is to read/copy Drive files with the gws API (files get alt=media). stat() is fine. Index Drive by name+size only, move with the gws CLI (Drive MCP moves get blocked), skip 02_Raw_Tagging"

---

Opening files through `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…/My Drive/` hangs when the file is
not cached locally. Measured 2026-10-14: a sha256 walk of `_FROM_WORK_LAPTOP` sat 65 minutes with
0.2 s of CPU, frozen on a `.lock` file. A hash walk of the OneDrive mirror did the same (that
folder is 0 KB on disk — all cloud placeholders). `stat()` and `os.walk` are fine: five Drive
folders, 76k files, 10 seconds by name+size.

One folder hangs even on listing: `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/02_Raw_Tagging`
(thousands of face images). Skip it in any Drive walk.

**DEFAULT (Eric, 2026-10-17): read or copy any Drive file through the gws API, never through the
mount.** The mount is for `ls`/`stat` only. 2026-10-17 a `cp` of a 24 MB workbook sat at 0 bytes, twice,
even after Eric quit and reopened Google Drive; the API pulled it in seconds:
- Find the id: `gws drive files list --params '{"q":"name contains '\''<name>'\'' and trashed=false","fields":"files(id,name,size,parents)"}'`
- Download: `gws drive files get --params '{"fileId":"<id>","alt":"media"}' -o <local path>`
- Same name can exist twice (a copy in `Send/`); pick by `parents`.

**How to apply:**
- Compare Drive copies by `(basename, size)`, never by content. `~/DEV/_INBOX/tools/drain_diff.py --names-only`.
- Move or rename Drive folders with the Drive MCP (`update_file` with `parentId`) — server-side, instant,
  no FUSE. Never `mv` a big tree through the mount.
- Put any Drive walk under a wall-clock watchdog; a hang shows as elapsed time with no CPU.
- Related: [[drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop]] (rsync re-sends), [[rea-ghidra-setup-traps]] (Drive reads hang R).

**Moving Drive items (2026-10-14 evening):** the Claude Code permission classifier can block the Drive MCP
`update_file` move as "Modify Shared Resources" even after it has worked in the same session. The gws CLI
(`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`, Drive scope granted) does the same server-side move from the shell and is not blocked:
`gws drive files update --params '{"fileId":"<id>","addParents":"<new>","removeParents":"<old>","fields":"id,name,parents"}' --json '{}'`.
Uploads with `--upload` must name a file under the current directory (`cd` to the job tmp dir first).

# Why Baylor's own players disagree most (2026-10-19)

Open question from the 2026-09-16 validation run: Keaton Thomas (AL to LIM),
DJ Coleman (QS to FRP, Player Impact 96) and DJ Lagway (AL to NGE) are the
three biggest misses. This note checks each player against the FBS Telemetry
exports for 2024, 2025 and 2026 (Drive `_exports/2024_baseline`,
`2025_baseline`, `2026_asof_2026-10-06`; read through the gws API). Same
PlayerId in every season. Percentiles are within Telemetry's position group.

**Short answer: there is no single cause. Each player misses for a different
reason, and two of the three would be caught by looking at more than one
season.**

## Keaton Thomas (ILB): one down season, and his value was in coverage

| Season | Team | Snaps | Tackling | Run D | Burst | CoD | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Baylor | 798 | 94 | 53 | 72 | 94 | 86 |
| 2025 | Baylor | 806 | 66 | 41 | 67 | 26 | 66 |
| 2026 | Ole Miss | 209 | 93 | 44 | 95 | n/a | 90 |

- 2025 was his worst season of the three. The validation used only 2025.
  In 2024 he had 2 elite counted traits (Tackling, CoD); in 2026 he has 2
  (Tackling, Burst) and Player Impact 90.
- His 2025 strengths are coverage stats that the 7 counted OB-LB traits do
  not include: Ball Hawk 93, Penalty 100, Comp Rate Over Expected 72.
- He transferred to Ole Miss for 2026.

## DJ Coleman (FS / slot): graded against the wrong group

| Season | Team | Group | Snaps | Play Speed | Deep Speed | Tackling | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Baylor | SAF (FS) | 235 | 100 | 100 | 91 | 58 |
| 2025 | Baylor | CB (SCB) | 605 | 47 | 49 | 100 | 96 |
| 2026 | Florida | SAF (FS) | 275 | 85 | 87 | n/a | 89 |

- In 2025 Telemetry put him in the CB group as a slot corner, so every
  percentile compares him to corners. His speed and CoD (8) look poor
  against corners. As a safety in 2024 and 2026 his speed is 85 to 100.
- Player Impact 96 was the right signal. The 90+ Impact alert already
  catches him; elite share does not.
- He transferred to Florida for 2026, back at free safety.

## DJ Lagway (QB): the data agrees with itself for three seasons

| Season | Team | Snaps | Accuracy | INT Avoid. | Adj Throw Vel | Passing Eff. | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Florida | 432 | 42 | 31 | 6 | 51 | 77 |
| 2025 | Florida | 736 | 50 | 14 | 11 | 12 | 76 |
| 2026 | Baylor | 261 | 4 | 43 | 54 | 23 | 63 |

- No season shows AL-level passing. 2026 at Baylor is the lowest yet on
  Accuracy and Player Impact.
- This is not a data error. The AL grade carries something Telemetry does
  not measure (projection, pedigree, traits not in the export). This is a
  question for staff, not a workbook fix.

## What this means for the workbook

1. **Use more than one season.** A prior-season check would have caught
   Thomas (2024) and Coleman (2024 as FS). Today the board reads one season.
2. **Flag position-group moves.** A player whose group changed between
   seasons (FS to SCB) is being compared to a different population.
3. **Keep Player Impact as a backstop.** The Impact alert caught Coleman.
   This matches Eric's 2026-10-19 rule that Player Impact wins over Size.

None of these is built. Items 1 and 2 are proposals for a later workbook.

- In 2024 he scored Tackling 94 and CoD 94, with Player Impact 86.

- In 2026 he is at Ole Miss and back up: Tackling 93, Burst 95, Player Impact 90.
- His 2025 strengths were in coverage (Ball Hawk 93). Coverage is not one of the 7 LB traits we count.

**DJ Coleman: compared to the wrong group.**
- In 2025 Telemetry listed him as a slot corner. That means it compared his speed to cornerbacks, so he looked slow.
- He is a safety. As a free safety in 2024 (Baylor) and 2026 (Florida), his speed scores are 85 to 100.
- His Player Impact of 96 was the right signal. The Impact alert already catches him.

**DJ Lagway: the data agrees with itself.**

# 2026-10-17 020 (new Telemetry traits, PROJECT flag): Mac test build

## What and why

A colleague asked where Telemetry's new OL traits fit the grading scale, and
whether weight ranges overlook young "project" players. Eric asked for the
answer and then a 020 build.

- Telemetry added 5 Player Traits (7 group-columns): Pull Agility and Perimeter
  Speed (OT, IOL); Closing and Reaction Time (OB-LB); Targeted Coverage,
  Closing, Reaction Time (CB, SAF). Advanced Stats unchanged. Definitions from
  Telemetry tooltips and the confirmed crosswalk: `docs/2026-10-17-new-telemetry-traits.md`.
- Perimeter Speed is "straight line speed", so it supports Speed (Play-speed),
  not Foot speed / Redirect as the colleague proposed.
- All 5 are secondary metrics (after BT, outside P:AI): elite share unchanged.
- Weight: SIZE (data) never scores 1 on weight (weight only decides 9 vs 3;
  REVIEW? never reads SIZE). Eric chose an information-only PROJECT column:
  HT at the 9 line, WT under the band (and > 0), Elig Yrs >= SETTINGS B59 (3).
- Build on the Mac as a TEST copy; it goes to Send/ only after Mauro's Windows
  Refresh All works.

1. `scripts/patch_mashup.py`: rewrites Formulas/Section1.m inside the
   DataMashup (customXml/item1.xml) from `scripts/powerquery/*.m`. Only that
   zip part changes.

   Refresh All. On this Mac the refresh never runs (no error, query engine
   idle), so the shipped file holds 019's 2025 data unchanged. The final file
   was saved by hand-run helpers after the script was stopped; the PROJECT fill
   was redone (Mac Excel ignores a formula written over an existing one; clear
   first, write AR5, copy down). The script now does that.
3. Read 019 with `gws drive files get ... alt=media` (the Drive mount hangs on
   large files, even after a Drive restart). Upload with `gws drive files create --upload`.

## Verification

- `check_workbook.py` on 020: ALL CHECKS PASS (12,029 rows, 2,121 REVIEW); 8 CF rules, same as 019.

"""add-new-traits: build 020 on the Mac from patch_mashup.py output (Mac Excel via xlwings).

Telemetry added five Player Traits in October 2026 (Pull Agility, Perimeter
Speed on OT/IOL; Closing, Reaction Time on OB-LB; Targeted Coverage, Closing,
Reaction Time on CB/SAF). Decisions: docs/2026-10-17-new-telemetry-traits.md.
020 changes:
- Power Query Stage (done by patch_mashup.py): the five land on PORTAL INPUT
  after BT as secondary metrics; a Mac folder path (/...) also loads.
- CROSSWALK: the five added as secondary metrics on the factors Eric confirmed.
- METRIC GLOSSARY: five rows with Telemetry's own definitions.
- SETTINGS row 59: PROJECT minimum Elig Yrs (3).
- REVIEW BOARD AR "Project": PROJECT when height is at the position's 9 line,
  weight is under the ideal band and Elig Yrs is at least SETTINGS B59.
  Information only: no other formula reads it, SIZE (data) is unchanged.
- README: a note on the above.
The workbook is refreshed on the 44 2025 CSVs 019 shipped with, so every
player value should be unchanged; the export folder cell is left empty.

Mac only. Refuses to overwrite --out.

Usage:
  uv run --with xlwings python scripts/add_new_traits.py --src "<work>/020_step1.xlsx" \
      --out "<work>/020 ....xlsx" --stage "<work>/load_2025"
"""

import argparse
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

LAST_RB_ROW = 20004

# (CROSSWALK row, new Secondary metrics F, text appended to Data flag rule H or None)
CROSSWALK = [
    (31, "Deceleration (WR, CB, S); Pull Agility (OT)", None),
    (33, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (41, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (43, "Pull Agility, Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", None),
    (75, "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness, Closing", None),
    (82, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (84, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
    (90, "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD, Closing", None),
    (91, "Reaction Time, Target Rate, EPA Per Target", None),
    (98, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (100, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
]
# Row 33 / 41 checks: the F text these rows carried in 019.
CROSSWALK_WAS = {31: "Deceleration (WR, CB, S)", 33: "Movement", 41: "Movement",
                 43: "Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", 75: "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness",
                 82: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 84: "Completion Rate Over Expected",
                 90: "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD", 91: "Target Rate, EPA Per Target",
                 98: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 100: "Completion Rate Over Expected"}

GLOSSARY = [
    ["Pull Agility", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Pulling / 2nd Level (OG, C); Athletic Flexibility (OT). Secondary."],
    ["Perimeter Speed", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's straight line speed. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Speed (critical), OL. Secondary."],
    ["Targeted Coverage", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF",
     "Telemetry: the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. Added 2026.",
     "Man-to-Man Coverage (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
    ["Closing", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: a defender's ability to close on the ball in the air, as primary and secondary defender. Added 2026.",
     "Ball Skills (CB, STAR); Range (SAF); Lateral Quickness / Range (LB). Secondary."],
    ["Reaction Time", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it is thrown. Added 2026; few players scored.",
     "Key & Diagnose (SAF); Ball Skills (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
]

SETTING = ["PROJECT flag: minimum Elig Yrs", 3,
           "REVIEW BOARD Project column: PROJECT when height is at the 9 line, weight is under the ideal band and "
           "Elig Yrs is at least this. Information only; SIZE (data) is unchanged (weight only decides 9 vs 3)."]

P = "'PORTAL INPUT'!"
LOOK = "MATCH({p}B5,SETTINGS!$A$27:$A$38,0)".format(p=P)
PROJECT = (f'=IF({P}A5="","",IFERROR(IF(AND(ISNUMBER({P}E5),ISNUMBER({P}F5),'
           f'{P}E5>=INDEX(SETTINGS!$B$27:$B$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'{P}F5>0,{P}F5<INDEX(SETTINGS!$D$27:$D$38,{LOOK}),'  # WT 0 = missing
           f'N({P}G5)>=SETTINGS!$B$59),"PROJECT",""),""))')

README_ADD = (" 020: Telemetry's 2026 traits (Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed, Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction "
              "Time) load after BT as secondary metrics; they do not change elite share. REVIEW BOARD column AR "
              "flags PROJECT: tall enough for a 9, under the weight band, Elig Yrs at least SETTINGS B59.")


def wait_refresh(ud, before, timeout=1200):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        time.sleep(10)
        try:
            now = ud.range("B16").value
        except Exception:  # Excel answers -1728 while a refresh is running
            continue
        if now and now != before:
            time.sleep(10)
            return time.time() - t0
    raise SystemExit("Refresh did not finish")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
        rb.range("AR4").value = "Project"
        # Mac Excel silently ignores a formula written over the copied one, and a
        # 20,000-cell .formula write: clear, write AR5, copy it down.
        rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").clear_contents()
        rb.range("AR5").value = PROJECT
        rb.range("AR5").copy(rb.range(f"AR6:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}"))
        app.calculate()
        flagged = sum(1 for v in rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").value if v == "PROJECT")
        print(f"PROJECT rows: {flagged}")

        readme = wb.sheets["README"]
        used = readme.used_range
        hits = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(used.value) for c, v in enumerate(row)
                if isinstance(v, str) and "PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query" in v]
        if len(hits) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"README DATA LOAD note found {len(hits)} times")
        addr = used[hits[0][0], hits[0][1]].address
        txt = readme.range(addr).value
        if README_ADD.strip() not in txt:
            readme.range(addr).value = txt + README_ADD

        ud = wb.sheets["UPDATE DATA"]
        folder = wb.names["LoadFolder"].refers_to_range
        folder.value = str(Path(args.stage)) + "/"
        before = ud.range("B16").value
        wb.api.refresh_all()
        print(f"Refresh All: {wait_refresh(ud, before):.0f} s")
        folder.value = ""  # shipped empty
        for item, value in ud.range("A16:B26").value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:160]}")
        wb.save()
        wb.close()
    finally:
        app.quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
      21 scripts/powerquery/LoadStatus.m
       5 scripts/powerquery/PortalInput.m
     276 scripts/powerquery/Stage.m
     302 total

    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
        rb.range("AR4").value = "Project"
        # Mac Excel silently ignores a formula written over the copied one, and a
        # 20,000-cell .formula write: clear, write AR5, copy it down.
        rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").clear_contents()
        rb.range("AR5").value = PROJECT
        rb.range("AR5").copy(rb.range(f"AR6:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}"))
        app.calculate()
        flagged = sum(1 for v in rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").value if v == "PROJECT")
        print(f"PROJECT rows: {flagged}")

        readme = wb.sheets["README"]
        used = readme.used_range
        hits = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(used.value) for c, v in enumerate(row)
                if isinstance(v, str) and "PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query" in v]
        if len(hits) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"README DATA LOAD note found {len(hits)} times")
        addr = used[hits[0][0], hits[0][1]].address
        txt = readme.range(addr).value
        if README_ADD.strip() not in txt:
            readme.range(addr).value = txt + README_ADD

        ud = wb.sheets["UPDATE DATA"]
        folder = wb.names["LoadFolder"].refers_to_range
        folder.value = str(Path(args.stage)) + "/"
        before = ud.range("B16").value
        wb.api.refresh_all()
        print(f"Refresh All: {wait_refresh(ud, before):.0f} s")
        folder.value = ""  # shipped empty
        for item, value in ud.range("A16:B26").value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:160]}")
        wb.save()
        wb.close()
    finally:
        app.quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")

"""Load Telemetry leaderboard CSV exports into a new numbered grading workbook.

Reconstructs the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, for leaderboard exports
(Leaderboards > Player Traits / Advanced Stats > Download CSV) rather than the
Transfer Portal scrape.

Two stages:

1. Stage (always): read every CSV in --csv-dir, join Player Traits and Advanced
   Stats rows on PlayerId, map headers onto the template's PORTAL INPUT row 4,
   and write a staging CSV plus a report. No Excel needed.
2. Build (--out): copy the template to a NEW file and write PORTAL INPUT through
   Excel COM, so formulas, fonts and conditional formatting survive. openpyxl is
   used only to read; saving through it strips the conditional formatting.

The algorithm is not changed here. PORTAL INPUT columns A:BO keep their meaning,
so REVIEW BOARD formulas, traits graded and elite share are untouched. Extra
fields (PlayerId, raw position code, Elusiveness, source) go in columns after
Notes.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
      --csv-dir <folder of CSVs> --template <003 xlsx> --stage-dir <folder> ^
      [--min-elig 2] [--out <new 008 xlsx>]
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json

39	        "POSITION MAP", "PORTAL INPUT", "REVIEW BOARD"]
40	OPTIONAL_TABS = ["BENCHMARK PROFILES"]  # 012 on (add_benchmark.py); last if present
41	SETTINGS_LABELS = {

43	    "A8": "Speed alert", "A9": "Review trigger", "A10": "Minimum graded traits",

48	INPUT_HEADERS = {"A": "Player", "B": "Pos (Telemetry)", "H": "Snaps", "P": "Play Speed",
49	                 "Q": "Deep Speed", "AC": "Tackling", "AD": "Accuracy",
50	                 "AI": "Target Selection", "AJ": "Player Impact", "BN": "Penalty Drawn",
51	                 "BO": "Notes", "BP": "PlayerId"}
52	BOARD_HEADERS = ["Player", "Pos", "Baylor tab", "Snaps", "Sample", "Traits graded",
53	                 "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "REVIEW?",
54	                 "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Impact alert", "Low Impact alert"]
55	KEY_FORMULA_PARTS = {
56	    "E": ["SETTINGS!$B$7"],
57	    "J": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$A$17", "SETTINGS!$A$18", "SETTINGS!$A$19", "SETTINGS!$A$20"],
58	    "K": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$B$9", 'L5="Y"', 'N5="Y"', "F5=0"],
59	    "L": ["SETTINGS!$B$8", "'PORTAL INPUT'!P5", "'PORTAL INPUT'!Q5"],
60	    "N": ["SETTINGS!$B$11", "'PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5"],
61	    "O": ["SETTINGS!$B$12", 'K5="Y"'],

63	RECOMPUTED = ["Traits graded", "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band",
64	              "Sample", "Speed alert", "Impact alert", "REVIEW?", "Low Impact alert"]
65	REF = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z_$])(\$?)([A-Z]{1,3})(\$?)(\d+)(?![\d(])")
66	
67	
68	def col(letter):
69	    n = 0
70	    for ch in letter:

72	    return n - 1
73	
74	
75	def shift(formula, rows):
76	    """Row 5 formula -> the same formula written for a later row."""
77	    def repl(m):
78	        if m.group(3):
79	            return m.group(0)
80	        return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}{m.group(3)}{int(m.group(4)) + rows}"
81	    return REF.sub(repl, formula)
82	
83	
84	def num(v):
85	    return v if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) else None
86	
87	
88	def blank(v):
89	    return v is None or v == ""
90	
91	
92	class Report:
93	    def __init__(self, max_report):
94	        self.results, self.max = [], max_report
95	
96	    def add(self, name, problems, detail=""):
97	        ok = not problems
98	        self.results.append(ok)
99	        print(f"[{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}{': ' + detail if detail else ''}")
100	        for p in problems[:self.max]:
101	            print(f"        {p}")
102	        if len(problems) > self.max:
103	            print(f"        ... {len(problems) - self.max} more")
104	
105	
106	def cond_format(path):
107	    """Count conditionalFormatting blocks on REVIEW BOARD straight from the xlsx XML."""
108	    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
109	        wb_xml = z.read("xl/workbook.xml").decode("utf8")
110	        rels = z.read("xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels").decode("utf8")
111	        rid = re.search(r'<sheet [^>]*name="REVIEW BOARD"[^>]*r:id="(rId\d+)"', wb_xml).group(1)
112	        target = re.search(rf'Id="{rid}"[^>]*Target="([^"]+)"', rels) or \
113	            re.search(rf'Target="([^"]+)"[^>]*Id="{rid}"', rels)
114	        sheet = z.read("xl/" + target.group(1).lstrip("/").replace("xl/", "")).decode("utf8")
115	    return re.findall(r'<conditionalFormatting sqref="([^"]+)"', sheet)
116	
117	
118	def main():
119	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
120	    ap.add_argument("workbook")
121	    ap.add_argument("--max-report", type=int, default=10)
122	    args = ap.parse_args()
123	    rep = Report(args.max_report)
124	
125	    wf = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True)
126	    wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True, data_only=True)
127	
128	    # 014 (self-service load) adds UPDATE DATA after README and a hidden BENCHMARK IDS last.
129	    self_service = TABS[:1] + ["UPDATE DATA"] + TABS[1:] + OPTIONAL_TABS + ["BENCHMARK IDS"]
130	    # 015 adds HONORS BENCHMARK after BENCHMARK PROFILES (add_honors_benchmark.py).
131	    honors = self_service[:-1] + ["HONORS BENCHMARK", "BENCHMARK IDS"]
132	    rep.add("tabs", [] if wf.sheetnames in (TABS, TABS + OPTIONAL_TABS, self_service, honors)
133	            else [f"found {wf.sheetnames}"])
134	
135	    sv = {c.coordinate: c.value for row in wv["SETTINGS"].iter_rows(min_row=1, max_row=21, max_col=3)
136	          for c in row if hasattr(c, "coordinate")}
137	    probs = [f"{cell} is {sv.get(cell)!r}, expected to start {label!r}"
138	             for cell, label in SETTINGS_LABELS.items() if not str(sv.get(cell) or "").startswith(label)]
139	    probs += [f"B{r} is {sv.get(f'B{r}')!r}, not a number" for r in range(5, 13) if num(sv.get(f"B{r}")) is None]
140	    probs += [f"{cell} band is {sv.get('B' + cell[1:])!r}, expected {band}"
141	              for cell, band in BANDS.items() if sv.get("B" + cell[1:]) != band or num(sv.get(cell)) is None]
142	    rep.add("settings", probs)
143	    S = {k: sv.get(k) for k in ("B5", "B6", "B7", "B8", "B9", "B10", "B11", "B12", "A17", "A18", "A19", "A20")}
144	
145	    inp_rows = wv["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
146	    inp_head = list(next(inp_rows))
147	    probs = [f"PORTAL INPUT {c}4 is {inp_head[col(c)]!r}, expected {h!r}"
148	             for c, h in INPUT_HEADERS.items() if col(c) >= len(inp_head) or inp_head[col(c)] != h]
149	    board_vals = wv["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
150	    board_head = list(next(board_vals))
151	    probs += [f"REVIEW BOARD column {i + 1} is {board_head[i]!r}, expected {h!r}"
152	              for i, h in enumerate(BOARD_HEADERS) if i >= len(board_head) or board_head[i] != h]
153	    rep.add("headers", probs)
154	    if probs:
155	        print("Stopping: layout is not the 009 layout, so later checks would be meaningless.")
156	        return 1
157	
158	    # Every row's formula, written back as if it were row 5. The most common version
159	    # per column is the reference, so a hand edit is caught on any row, row 5 included.
160	    seen, rows_checked = {}, 0
161	    for row in wf["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=5):
162	        cells = [c for c in row if hasattr(c, "column_letter")]
163	        if not cells or blank(cells[0].value):
164	            continue
165	        rows_checked += 1
166	        r = cells[0].row
167	        for c in cells:
168	            v = c.value
169	            norm = shift(v, 5 - r) if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("=") else repr(v)
170	            seen.setdefault(c.column_letter, []).append((r, norm, v))
171	    base, drift = {}, []
172	    for letter, entries in seen.items():
173	        mode, n = Counter(e[1] for e in entries).most_common(1)[0]
174	        if not mode.startswith("="):
175	            continue
176	        base[letter] = mode
177	        drift += [f"{letter}{r} = {str(v)[:70]!r} (column formula differs here)"
178	                  for r, norm, v in entries if norm != mode]
179	    probs = [f"column {letter} formula missing {part!r}" for letter, parts in KEY_FORMULA_PARTS.items()
180	             for part in parts if part not in (base.get(letter) or "")]
181	    rep.add("formulas", probs + drift, f"{len(base)} formula columns x {rows_checked} rows")
182	
183	    board = [dict(zip(board_head, r)) for r in board_vals]
184	    inputs = [r for r in inp_rows]
185	    if board and all(r.get("Traits graded") is None for r in board[:200]):
186	        rep.add("calculated values", ["REVIEW BOARD has formulas but no calculated values: the file was "
187	                                      "saved outside Excel (openpyxl). Rebuild or open and save in Excel."])
188	        print("RESULT: FAILED")
189	        return 1
190	    errs = [f"row {i + 5} {k} = {v}" for i, row in enumerate(board) for k, v in row.items()
191	            if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("#")]
192	    rep.add("errors", errs)
193	
194	    sq = cond_format(args.workbook)
195	    probs = [] if sq else ["no conditional formatting on REVIEW BOARD (saved with openpyxl?)"]
196	    if sq and not any(s.startswith("L5:O") for s in sq):
197	        probs.append(f"alert highlight does not cover L:O; ranges {sq}")
198	    rep.add("cond-format", probs, f"{len(sq)} rules")
199	
200	    profiles = None
201	    if "Profile REVIEW" in board_head:
202	        srows = list(wv["SETTINGS"].iter_rows(min_row=44, max_row=58, max_col=12, values_only=True))
203	        profiles = {r[0]: r for r in srows[:12] if r[0]}
204	        prof_snaps, diamond_cut = num(srows[13][1]), num(srows[14][1])
205	        where = {h: j for j, h in enumerate(inp_head) if h}
206	
207	    def profile_flags(row, snaps):
208	        """Must-have 1/2, Profile, Diamond, Profile REVIEW for one PORTAL INPUT row."""
209	        p = profiles.get(row[col("B")])
210	        if p is None:
211	            return {k: None for k in ("Must-have 1", "Must-have 2", "Profile", "Diamond signal", "Profile REVIEW")}
212	        val = lambda name: num(row[where[name]])  # noqa: E731
213	
214	        def status(name, floor, target):
215	            v = val(name)
216	            return "NO DATA" if v is None else "TARGET" if v >= target else "FLOOR" if v >= floor else "BELOW"
217	        m1, m2 = status(p[1], p[2], p[3]), status(p[4], p[5], p[6])
218	        hit = ("TARGET", "FLOOR")
219	        prof = ("BOTH-T" if m1 == m2 == "TARGET" else "BOTH" if m1 in hit and m2 in hit
220	                else "ONE" if m1 in hit or m2 in hit else "NO DATA" if m1 == m2 == "NO DATA" else "NONE")
221	        main, backup = val(p[7]), val(p[9])
222	        diamond = "Y" if main is not None and backup is not None and main < p[8] and backup >= diamond_cut else None
223	        path = "Y" if p[11] == "Y" and prof in ("BOTH", "BOTH-T") and snaps >= prof_snaps else None
224	        return {"Must-have 1": m1, "Must-have 2": m2, "Profile": prof, "Diamond signal": diamond,
225	                "Profile REVIEW": path}
226	
227	    P, Q, H, AJ = col("P"), col("Q"), col("H"), col("AJ")
228	    traits = range(col("P"), col("AI") + 1)
229	    mism, counts = Counter(), Counter()
230	    examples = []
231	    for i, (row, got) in enumerate(zip(inputs, board)):
232	        if blank(row[0]):
233	            continue
234	        vals = [num(row[j]) for j in traits]
235	        graded = [v for v in vals if v is not None]
236	        F = len(graded)
237	        G = sum(v >= S["B5"] for v in graded)
238	        D = sum(v < S["B6"] for v in graded)
239	        share = G / F if F else None
240	        if F == 0:
241	            band = "NO DATA"
242	        elif F < S["B10"]:
243	            band = "THIN"
244	        elif share >= S["A17"]:
245	            band = "AA"
246	        elif share >= S["A18"]:
247	            band = "AL"
248	        elif share >= S["A19"]:
249	            band = "QS"

254	        sample = "LOW SAMPLE" if (num(row[H]) or 0) < S["B7"] else "OK"

256	        impact = "Y" if not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) >= S["B11"] else None
257	        extra = profile_flags(row, num(row[H]) or 0) if profiles is not None else {}
258	        path = extra.get("Profile REVIEW")

260	        low = "Y" if review and not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) <= S["B12"] else None
261	        want = {"Traits graded": F, "Elite traits": G, "Deficiencies": D, "Elite share": share,

from collections import Counter

import openpyxl

TABS = ["README", "SETTINGS", "GRADE SCALE", "METRIC GLOSSARY", "CROSSWALK",
        "POSITION MAP", "PORTAL INPUT", "REVIEW BOARD"]
OPTIONAL_TABS = ["BENCHMARK PROFILES"]  # 012 on (add_benchmark.py); last if present
SETTINGS_LABELS = {
    "A5": "Elite percentile", "A6": "Poor percentile", "A7": "Minimum snaps",
    "A8": "Speed alert", "A9": "Review trigger", "A10": "Minimum graded traits",
    "A11": "Player Impact alert", "A12": "Low Impact alert",
    "A16": "Minimum elite share",
}
BANDS = {"A17": "AA", "A18": "AL", "A19": "QS", "A20": "FRP"}
INPUT_HEADERS = {"A": "Player", "B": "Pos (Telemetry)", "H": "Snaps", "P": "Play Speed",
                 "Q": "Deep Speed", "AC": "Tackling", "AD": "Accuracy",
                 "AI": "Target Selection", "AJ": "Player Impact", "BN": "Penalty Drawn",
                 "BO": "Notes", "BP": "PlayerId"}
BOARD_HEADERS = ["Player", "Pos", "Baylor tab", "Snaps", "Sample", "Traits graded",
                 "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "REVIEW?",
                 "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Impact alert", "Low Impact alert"]
KEY_FORMULA_PARTS = {
    "E": ["SETTINGS!$B$7"],
    "J": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$A$17", "SETTINGS!$A$18", "SETTINGS!$A$19", "SETTINGS!$A$20"],
    "K": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$B$9", 'L5="Y"', 'N5="Y"', "F5=0"],
    "L": ["SETTINGS!$B$8", "'PORTAL INPUT'!P5", "'PORTAL INPUT'!Q5"],
    "N": ["SETTINGS!$B$11", "'PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5"],
    "O": ["SETTINGS!$B$12", 'K5="Y"'],
}
RECOMPUTED = ["Traits graded", "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band",
              "Sample", "Speed alert", "Impact alert", "REVIEW?", "Low Impact alert"]
REF = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z_$])(\$?)([A-Z]{1,3})(\$?)(\d+)(?![\d(])")


def col(letter):
    n = 0
    for ch in letter:
        n = n * 26 + ord(ch) - 64
    return n - 1


def shift(formula, rows):
    """Row 5 formula -> the same formula written for a later row."""
    def repl(m):
        if m.group(3):
            return m.group(0)
        return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}{m.group(3)}{int(m.group(4)) + rows}"
    return REF.sub(repl, formula)


def num(v):
    return v if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) else None


def blank(v):
    return v is None or v == ""


class Report:
    def __init__(self, max_report):
        self.results, self.max = [], max_report

    def add(self, name, problems, detail=""):
        ok = not problems
        self.results.append(ok)
        print(f"[{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}{': ' + detail if detail else ''}")
        for p in problems[:self.max]:
            print(f"        {p}")
        if len(problems) > self.max:
            print(f"        ... {len(problems) - self.max} more")


def cond_format(path):
    """Count conditionalFormatting blocks on REVIEW BOARD straight from the xlsx XML."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        wb_xml = z.read("xl/workbook.xml").decode("utf8")
        rels = z.read("xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels").decode("utf8")
        rid = re.search(r'<sheet [^>]*name="REVIEW BOARD"[^>]*r:id="(rId\d+)"', wb_xml).group(1)
        target = re.search(rf'Id="{rid}"[^>]*Target="([^"]+)"', rels) or \
            re.search(rf'Target="([^"]+)"[^>]*Id="{rid}"', rels)
        sheet = z.read("xl/" + target.group(1).lstrip("/").replace("xl/", "")).decode("utf8")
    return re.findall(r'<conditionalFormatting sqref="([^"]+)"', sheet)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("workbook")
    ap.add_argument("--max-report", type=int, default=10)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rep = Report(args.max_report)

    wf = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True)
    wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True, data_only=True)

    # 014 (self-service load) adds UPDATE DATA after README and a hidden BENCHMARK IDS last.
    self_service = TABS[:1] + ["UPDATE DATA"] + TABS[1:] + OPTIONAL_TABS + ["BENCHMARK IDS"]
    # 015 adds HONORS BENCHMARK after BENCHMARK PROFILES (add_honors_benchmark.py).
    honors = self_service[:-1] + ["HONORS BENCHMARK", "BENCHMARK IDS"]
    rep.add("tabs", [] if wf.sheetnames in (TABS, TABS + OPTIONAL_TABS, self_service, honors)
            else [f"found {wf.sheetnames}"])

    sv = {c.coordinate: c.value for row in wv["SETTINGS"].iter_rows(min_row=1, max_row=21, max_col=3)
          for c in row if hasattr(c, "coordinate")}
    probs = [f"{cell} is {sv.get(cell)!r}, expected to start {label!r}"
             for cell, label in SETTINGS_LABELS.items() if not str(sv.get(cell) or "").startswith(label)]
    probs += [f"B{r} is {sv.get(f'B{r}')!r}, not a number" for r in range(5, 13) if num(sv.get(f"B{r}")) is None]
    probs += [f"{cell} band is {sv.get('B' + cell[1:])!r}, expected {band}"
              for cell, band in BANDS.items() if sv.get("B" + cell[1:]) != band or num(sv.get(cell)) is None]
    rep.add("settings", probs)
    S = {k: sv.get(k) for k in ("B5", "B6", "B7", "B8", "B9", "B10", "B11", "B12", "A17", "A18", "A19", "A20")}

    inp_rows = wv["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    inp_head = list(next(inp_rows))
    probs = [f"PORTAL INPUT {c}4 is {inp_head[col(c)]!r}, expected {h!r}"
             for c, h in INPUT_HEADERS.items() if col(c) >= len(inp_head) or inp_head[col(c)] != h]
    board_vals = wv["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board_head = list(next(board_vals))
    probs += [f"REVIEW BOARD column {i + 1} is {board_head[i]!r}, expected {h!r}"
              for i, h in enumerate(BOARD_HEADERS) if i >= len(board_head) or board_head[i] != h]
    rep.add("headers", probs)
    if probs:
        print("Stopping: layout is not the 009 layout, so later checks would be meaningless.")
        return 1

    # Every row's formula, written back as if it were row 5. The most common version
    # per column is the reference, so a hand edit is caught on any row, row 5 included.
    seen, rows_checked = {}, 0
    for row in wf["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=5):
        cells = [c for c in row if hasattr(c, "column_letter")]
        if not cells or blank(cells[0].value):
            continue
        rows_checked += 1
        r = cells[0].row
        for c in cells:
            v = c.value
            norm = shift(v, 5 - r) if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("=") else repr(v)
            seen.setdefault(c.column_letter, []).append((r, norm, v))
    base, drift = {}, []
    for letter, entries in seen.items():
        mode, n = Counter(e[1] for e in entries).most_common(1)[0]
        if not mode.startswith("="):
            continue
        base[letter] = mode
        drift += [f"{letter}{r} = {str(v)[:70]!r} (column formula differs here)"
                  for r, norm, v in entries if norm != mode]
    probs = [f"column {letter} formula missing {part!r}" for letter, parts in KEY_FORMULA_PARTS.items()
             for part in parts if part not in (base.get(letter) or "")]
    rep.add("formulas", probs + drift, f"{len(base)} formula columns x {rows_checked} rows")

    board = [dict(zip(board_head, r)) for r in board_vals]
    inputs = [r for r in inp_rows]
    if board and all(r.get("Traits graded") is None for r in board[:200]):
        rep.add("calculated values", ["REVIEW BOARD has formulas but no calculated values: the file was "
                                      "saved outside Excel (openpyxl). Rebuild or open and save in Excel."])
        print("RESULT: FAILED")
        return 1
    errs = [f"row {i + 5} {k} = {v}" for i, row in enumerate(board) for k, v in row.items()
            if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("#")]
    rep.add("errors", errs)

    sq = cond_format(args.workbook)
    probs = [] if sq else ["no conditional formatting on REVIEW BOARD (saved with openpyxl?)"]
    if sq and not any(s.startswith("L5:O") for s in sq):
        probs.append(f"alert highlight does not cover L:O; ranges {sq}")
    rep.add("cond-format", probs, f"{len(sq)} rules")

    profiles = None
    if "Profile REVIEW" in board_head:
        srows = list(wv["SETTINGS"].iter_rows(min_row=44, max_row=58, max_col=12, values_only=True))
        profiles = {r[0]: r for r in srows[:12] if r[0]}
        prof_snaps, diamond_cut = num(srows[13][1]), num(srows[14][1])
        where = {h: j for j, h in enumerate(inp_head) if h}

    def profile_flags(row, snaps):
        """Must-have 1/2, Profile, Diamond, Profile REVIEW for one PORTAL INPUT row."""
        p = profiles.get(row[col("B")])
        if p is None:
            return {k: None for k in ("Must-have 1", "Must-have 2", "Profile", "Diamond signal", "Profile REVIEW")}
        val = lambda name: num(row[where[name]])  # noqa: E731

        def status(name, floor, target):
            v = val(name)
            return "NO DATA" if v is None else "TARGET" if v >= target else "FLOOR" if v >= floor else "BELOW"
        m1, m2 = status(p[1], p[2], p[3]), status(p[4], p[5], p[6])
        hit = ("TARGET", "FLOOR")
        prof = ("BOTH-T" if m1 == m2 == "TARGET" else "BOTH" if m1 in hit and m2 in hit
                else "ONE" if m1 in hit or m2 in hit else "NO DATA" if m1 == m2 == "NO DATA" else "NONE")
        main, backup = val(p[7]), val(p[9])
        diamond = "Y" if main is not None and backup is not None and main < p[8] and backup >= diamond_cut else None
        path = "Y" if p[11] == "Y" and prof in ("BOTH", "BOTH-T") and snaps >= prof_snaps else None
        return {"Must-have 1": m1, "Must-have 2": m2, "Profile": prof, "Diamond signal": diamond,
                "Profile REVIEW": path}

    P, Q, H, AJ = col("P"), col("Q"), col("H"), col("AJ")
    traits = range(col("P"), col("AI") + 1)
    mism, counts = Counter(), Counter()
    examples = []
    for i, (row, got) in enumerate(zip(inputs, board)):
        if blank(row[0]):
            continue
        vals = [num(row[j]) for j in traits]
        graded = [v for v in vals if v is not None]
        F = len(graded)
        G = sum(v >= S["B5"] for v in graded)
        D = sum(v < S["B6"] for v in graded)
        share = G / F if F else None
        if F == 0:
            band = "NO DATA"
        elif F < S["B10"]:
            band = "THIN"
        elif share >= S["A17"]:
            band = "AA"
        elif share >= S["A18"]:
            band = "AL"
        elif share >= S["A19"]:
            band = "QS"
        elif share >= S["A20"]:
            band = "FRP"
        else:
            band = "NGE" if D >= G + 2 else "LIM"
        sample = "LOW SAMPLE" if (num(row[H]) or 0) < S["B7"] else "OK"
        speed = "Y" if max(num(row[P]) or 0, num(row[Q]) or 0) >= S["B8"] else None
        impact = "Y" if not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) >= S["B11"] else None
        extra = profile_flags(row, num(row[H]) or 0) if profiles is not None else {}
        path = extra.get("Profile REVIEW")
        review = "Y" if F > 0 and ((F >= S["B10"] and share >= S["B9"]) or speed or impact or path) else None
        low = "Y" if review and not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) <= S["B12"] else None
        want = {"Traits graded": F, "Elite traits": G, "Deficiencies": D, "Elite share": share,
                "Projected band": band, "Sample": sample, "Speed alert": speed,
                "Impact alert": impact, "REVIEW?": review, "Low Impact alert": low, **extra}
        counts["rows"] += 1
        counts["REVIEW"] += review == "Y"
        for k in RECOMPUTED + list(extra):
            a, b = want[k], got.get(k)
            a = None if a in ("",) else a
            b = None if b in ("",) else b
            same = (abs(a - b) < 1e-9) if isinstance(a, float) and isinstance(b, (int, float)) else a == b
            if not same:
                mism[k] += 1
                if len(examples) < args.max_report:
                    examples.append(f"row {i + 5} {row[0]}: {k} workbook {b!r}, recomputed {a!r}")
    detail = f"{counts['rows']} rows, {counts['REVIEW']} REVIEW recomputed"
    rep.add("recompute", [f"{k}: {n} rows differ" for k, n in mism.items()] + examples, detail)

    ok = all(rep.results)
    print("RESULT:", "ALL CHECKS PASS" if ok else "FAILED")
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

ParseFile = (name as text, content as binary, idx as number) =>
        let
            raw = Table.PromoteHeaders(
                Csv.Document(content, [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]),
                [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
            cols = Table.ColumnNames(raw),
            blanks = Table.Buffer(Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = "" then null else _)),
            withPid = Table.SelectRows(blanks, each Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "PlayerId") <> null
                and Text.Trim(Record.Field(_, "PlayerId")) <> ""),
            derived = Table.AddColumn(withPid, "__derived", each [
                PlayerId = Text.Trim([PlayerId]),
                #"Pos (raw)" = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Pos."),
                #"HT (in)" = HeightInches(Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Height")),
                Hometown =
                    let town = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Hometown"),
                        st = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "State"),
                        stt = if st = null then "" else Text.Trim(st)
                    in if town = null then null else if stt <> "" then town & ", " & stt else town]),
            renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Table.RemoveColumns(derived, List.Intersect({cols, Special})),
                List.Select(Aliases, each List.Contains(cols, _{0}))),
            keep = List.Select(Table.ColumnNames(renamed), each List.Contains(Known, _)),
            base = Table.SelectColumns(renamed, keep & {"__derived"}),
            expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(base, "__derived",
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"},
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"}),
            indexed = Table.AddIndexColumn(expanded, "__row", 0, 1),
            tagged = Table.AddColumn(Table.AddColumn(indexed, "__idx", each idx), "__file", each name)
        in
            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name, Problems = CheckFile(cols, blanks)],

    Parsed = List.Transform(
        List.Positions(CheckedFiles[Name]),
        (i) => ParseFile(CheckedFiles{i}[Name], CheckedFiles{i}[Content], i)),

    Combined = Table.Buffer(Table.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Table]))),
    ValueCols = List.Difference(Table.ColumnNames(Combined), {"PlayerId", "__row", "__idx", "__file"}),

    // First non-blank value per column, in file-name order (as the Python loader).
    Grouped = Table.Group(Combined, {"PlayerId"}, {{"__rec", (g) =>
        let s = Table.Sort(g, {{"__idx", Order.Ascending}, {"__row", Order.Ascending}})
        in Record.FromList(
               List.Transform(ValueCols, (c) => List.First(List.RemoveNulls(Table.Column(s, c)))),
               ValueCols)
           & [#"Source files" = Text.Combine(List.Sort(List.Distinct(s[__file]), Comparer.Ordinal), "; ")]}}),
    Players = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Grouped), each [PlayerId = [PlayerId]] & [__rec]),
        null, MissingField.UseNull),

    BenchmarkIds = List.Buffer(
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = "BenchmarkIds"]}[Content][PlayerId] otherwise {}),

    Shaped = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Players), (r) =>
            let
                rawPos = Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Pos (raw)"),
                code = if rawPos = null then null else Record.FieldOrDefault(PosMap, rawPos, rawPos),
                withPos = r & [#"Pos (Telemetry)" = code],
                main = Record.FromList(
                    List.Transform(Headers, (h) =>
                        let v = Record.FieldOrDefault(withPos, h)
                        in if List.Contains(TextColumns, h) then v else Num(v)),
                    Headers),
                extra = [
                    PlayerId = r[PlayerId],
                    #"Pos (raw)" = rawPos,
                    Elusiveness = Num(Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Elusiveness")),
                    #"Source files" = r[#"Source files"],
                    #"Benchmark 2025" = if List.Contains(BenchmarkIds, r[PlayerId]) then "BENCHMARK" else null],
                newTraits = Record.FromList(
                    List.Transform(NewTraits, (h) => Num(Record.FieldOrDefault(r, h))), NewTraits)
            in main & extra & newTraits),
        Headers & Extras),

    Kept = Table.SelectRows(Shaped, each
        MinElig = null or ([Elig Yrs] is number and [Elig Yrs] >= MinElig)),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Kept, {
        {each if [#"Pos (Telemetry)"] = null then "" else Text.From([#"Pos (Telemetry)"]), Order.Ascending},
        {each if [Player] = null then "" else Text.From([Player]), Order.Ascending}}),

    AllHeaders = List.Distinct(List.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Headers]))),
