- Mac: `python3 board.py --background`

It reuses a board already running on this machine or starts one tied to this session, opens the page, and prints `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>`; put that line in the report. Eric's `pm` (shell) and `/pm` (Claude Code) run the same command later in the day.

Syncing git state is only half the job. The other half is loading the context that came with it, and nothing else does this — the SessionStart hook injects global memory, but project state lives in the repo, and Tier A project memory only crosses machines through the Step 1 mirror. Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Firecrawl provides web, developer, government, and research search, and executes catalogued Alexandria data providers. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes; authenticated searches also return matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and provider contracts; firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_scrape with a url retrieves one supplied page. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources in the web group and cannot be combined with other categories. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. Search and discovery tools are read-only and return ranked results. Billing: web, developer, and research search are billed per request; government search is free; Alexandria discovery (firecrawl_search with sources ["alexandria"] alone, and firecrawl_find_tools) is free; firecrawl_scrape is billed, as a page retrieval in url mode or at each executed capability's listed price in alexandria mode.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

# Why Baylor's own players disagree most (2026-10-19)

Open question from the 2026-09-16 validation run: Keaton Thomas (AL to LIM),
DJ Coleman (QS to FRP, Player Impact 96) and DJ Lagway (AL to NGE) are the
three biggest misses. This note checks each player against the FBS Telemetry
exports for 2024, 2025 and 2026 (Drive `_exports/2024_baseline`,
`2025_baseline`, `2026_asof_2026-10-06`; read through the gws API). Same
PlayerId in every season. Percentiles are within Telemetry's position group.

**Short answer: there is no single cause. Each player misses for a different
reason, and two of the three would be caught by looking at more than one
season.**

## Keaton Thomas (ILB): one down season, and his value was in coverage

| Season | Team | Snaps | Tackling | Run D | Burst | CoD | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Baylor | 798 | 94 | 53 | 72 | 94 | 86 |
| 2025 | Baylor | 806 | 66 | 41 | 67 | 26 | 66 |
| 2026 | Ole Miss | 209 | 93 | 44 | 95 | n/a | 90 |

- 2025 was his worst season of the three. The validation used only 2025.
  In 2024 he had 2 elite counted traits (Tackling, CoD); in 2026 he has 2
  (Tackling, Burst) and Player Impact 90.
- His 2025 strengths are coverage stats that the 7 counted OB-LB traits do
  not include: Ball Hawk 93, Penalty 100, Comp Rate Over Expected 72.
- He transferred to Ole Miss for 2026.

## DJ Coleman (FS / slot): graded against the wrong group

| Season | Team | Group | Snaps | Play Speed | Deep Speed | Tackling | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Baylor | SAF (FS) | 235 | 100 | 100 | 91 | 58 |
| 2025 | Baylor | CB (SCB) | 605 | 47 | 49 | 100 | 96 |
| 2026 | Florida | SAF (FS) | 275 | 85 | 87 | n/a | 89 |

- In 2025 Telemetry put him in the CB group as a slot corner, so every
  percentile compares him to corners. His speed and CoD (8) look poor
  against corners. As a safety in 2024 and 2026 his speed is 85 to 100.
- Player Impact 96 was the right signal. The 90+ Impact alert already
  catches him; elite share does not.
- He transferred to Florida for 2026, back at free safety.

## DJ Lagway (QB): the data agrees with itself for three seasons

| Season | Team | Snaps | Accuracy | INT Avoid. | Adj Throw Vel | Passing Eff. | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Florida | 432 | 42 | 31 | 6 | 51 | 77 |
| 2025 | Florida | 736 | 50 | 14 | 11 | 12 | 76 |
| 2026 | Baylor | 261 | 4 | 43 | 54 | 23 | 63 |

- No season shows AL-level passing. 2026 at Baylor is the lowest yet on
  Accuracy and Player Impact.
- This is not a data error. The AL grade carries something Telemetry does
  not measure (projection, pedigree, traits not in the export). This is a
  question for staff, not a workbook fix.

## What this means for the workbook

1. **Use more than one season.** A prior-season check would have caught
   Thomas (2024) and Coleman (2024 as FS). Today the board reads one season.
2. **Flag position-group moves.** A player whose group changed between
   seasons (FS to SCB) is being compared to a different population.
3. **Keep Player Impact as a backstop.** The Impact alert caught Coleman.
   This matches Eric's 2026-10-19 rule that Player Impact wins over Size.

None of these is built. Items 1 and 2 are proposals for a later workbook.

"""prior-season: build the PRIOR SEASON table (021) from Telemetry leaderboard CSVs.

One row per player per season, keyed Season & PlayerId ("2025THO169147"), with
the inputs REVIEW BOARD needs to judge last season the same way it judges this
one: position group, snaps, traits graded / elite / deficient, Player Impact and
the best of Play Speed / Deep Speed. Thresholds are NOT applied here, so the
workbook recomputes the prior band and prior REVIEW from SETTINGS.

Players are merged across files exactly as the Stage query does: files in name
order, first non-blank value per column per PlayerId. No Elig filter: last
season's eligibility is not this season's.

--check compares the rows for one season with a workbook loaded on that season
(020 ships loaded with 2025): every PlayerId on PORTAL INPUT must have the same
group, traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, Player Impact and speed.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/prior_season.py \
      --season 2024=<dir> --season 2025=<dir>,<dir> --out prior.csv \
      [--check <workbook.xlsx> --check-season 2025]
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from load_leaderboard import ALIASES, POSITION_CODES, number

# PORTAL INPUT P:AI, the counted traits (REVIEW BOARD F:I read these).
TRAITS = ["Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Ball Skills", "Run Blocking",
          "Pass Blocking", "Run Ability", "Tackle Breaking", "Get Off", "Pass Rush", "Run Defense",
          "Tackling", "Accuracy", "Max Throw Vel", "Adj Throw Vel", "INT Avoidance",
          "Pocket Awareness", "Target Selection"]
ELITE, POOR = 75, 25  # only for --check counts; the workbook uses SETTINGS B5/B6
COLUMNS = ["Key", "Season", "PlayerId", "Group", "Snaps", "Traits graded", "Elite traits",
           "Deficiencies", "Player Impact", "Max speed"]
KEY_OK = re.compile(r"^[0-9A-Z]+$")  # MATCH(...,1) on sorted keys needs Excel and Python to agree on order


def group(code):
    """Telemetry position code -> the group its percentiles compare against (OG and C are one IOL pool)."""
    code = POSITION_CODES.get(code, code)
    return "IOL" if code in ("OG", "C") else code


def merge(files):
    players = {}
    for path in sorted(files, key=lambda p: p.name):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                pid = (row.get("PlayerId") or "").strip()
                if not pid:
                    continue
                rec = players.setdefault(pid, {})
                for h, v in row.items():
                    h = ALIASES.get(h, h)
                    if h == "Pos (Telemetry)":
                        h = "Pos (raw)"
                    if rec.get(h) is None:
                        rec[h] = number(v) if h != "Pos (raw)" else ((v or "").strip() or None)
    return players


def season_rows(season, players):
    rows = []
    for pid, r in players.items():
        vals = [r.get(t) for t in TRAITS]
        graded = [v for v in vals if isinstance(v, (int, float))]
        pi = r.get("Player Impact")
        speeds = [v for v in (r.get("Play Speed"), r.get("Deep Speed")) if isinstance(v, (int, float))]
        rows.append({
            "Key": f"{season}{pid}", "Season": season, "PlayerId": pid,
            "Group": group(r.get("Pos (raw)")), "Snaps": r.get("Snaps") if isinstance(r.get("Snaps"), (int, float)) else 0,
            "Traits graded": len(graded), "Elite traits": sum(v >= ELITE for v in graded),
            "Deficiencies": sum(v < POOR for v in graded),
            "Player Impact": pi if isinstance(pi, (int, float)) else None,
            "Max speed": max(speeds) if speeds else None})
    return rows


def check(rows, workbook, season):
    import openpyxl
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(workbook, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    it = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    head = list(next(it))
    ix = {h: i for i, h in enumerate(head) if h}
    mine = {r["PlayerId"]: r for r in rows if r["Season"] == season}
    n, bad = 0, []
    for row in it:
        if not row[0]:
            continue
        n += 1
        pid = row[ix["PlayerId"]]
        m = mine.get(pid)
        if m is None:
            bad.append(f"{pid} {row[0]}: not in the table")
            continue
        graded = [row[ix[t]] for t in TRAITS if isinstance(row[ix[t]], (int, float))]
        speeds = [v for v in (row[ix["Play Speed"]], row[ix["Deep Speed"]]) if isinstance(v, (int, float))]
        pi = row[ix["Player Impact"]]
        want = {"Group": group(row[ix["Pos (Telemetry)"]]), "Traits graded": len(graded),
                "Elite traits": sum(v >= ELITE for v in graded), "Deficiencies": sum(v < POOR for v in graded),
                "Player Impact": pi if isinstance(pi, (int, float)) else None,
                "Max speed": max(speeds) if speeds else None}
        for k, v in want.items():
            if m[k] != v:
                bad.append(f"{pid} {row[0]}: {k} workbook {v!r}, table {m[k]!r}")
    print(f"check {season} vs {Path(workbook).name}: {n} PORTAL INPUT rows, {len(bad)} differences")
    for b in bad[:15]:
        print("  ", b)
    return not bad


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--season", action="append", required=True, help="YEAR=dir[,dir...]")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--check")
    ap.add_argument("--check-season", type=int)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rows = []
    for spec in args.season:
        year, dirs = spec.split("=", 1)
        files = [p for d in dirs.split(",") for p in Path(d).glob("*.csv")]
        season = season_rows(int(year), merge(files))
        print(f"{year}: {len(files)} files, {len(season)} players")
        rows += season
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["Key"])
    odd = [r["Key"] for r in rows if not KEY_OK.match(r["Key"])]
    if odd:
        raise SystemExit(f"{len(odd)} keys are not plain 0-9A-Z (sorted MATCH would break): {odd[:5]}")
    with open(args.out, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, COLUMNS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"wrote {len(rows)} rows to {args.out}")
    if args.check and not check(rows, args.check, args.check_season):
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def put(sheet, letter, last, formula):
    """Write a row-5 formula down a column the way Mac Excel accepts it.

    Mac Excel ignores a formula written over an existing one, a 20,000-cell
    .formula write (020 handoff) and any formula over 255 characters, all without
    an error: clear, write row 5, read it back, copy down.
    """
    if len(formula) > MAX_FORMULA:
        raise SystemExit(f"{sheet.name} {letter}: formula is {len(formula)} characters (Mac limit {MAX_FORMULA})")
    sheet.range(f"{letter}5:{letter}{last}").clear_contents()
    sheet.range(f"{letter}5").formula = formula
    if sheet.range(f"{letter}5").formula != formula:
        raise SystemExit(f"{sheet.name} {letter}5 did not take the formula: {sheet.range(f'{letter}5').formula!r}")
    sheet.range(f"{letter}5").copy(sheet.range(f"{letter}6:{letter}{last}"))

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.

The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
